messages:
mike: Ran an nsys profile on nightly with the fused flash-attn variant and saw an unusual SMEM affinity hotspot on SM 7.5. attaching quick notes.
anya: saw that too on small batch sizes?
mike: yes, mostly at batch=2 seq=1024, kv-cache enabled. Wall time jumps ~2.3x for certain microbatches.
kevin: can you paste the kernel timeline snippet?
mike: perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 (nsys -> perfetto conversion). Timeline shows repeated small flashes of flash_attn_fused_rw_kernel and a tight SMEM access band overlapping with kv_read/write kernels.
anya: that overlap is suspicious — could be SMEM bank thrash from our fused output plus KV writebacks.
dmitri: did you try setting SMEM allocator to per-warp? There was a recent heuristic change in kernel_selector that packs shared memory for faster latency but increases bank conflicts.
mike: I repro'd with a reduced run and dumped the nsys table:
```
# nsys stats (truncated)
Kernel                                      Calls  Total(ms)  Avg(us)  GPU(util)
flash_attn_fused_rw_kernel                   312    12450.23    39.92    68%
kv_cache_read_worker                          624    3102.12    4.97     45%
kv_cache_writeback                             78     985.44   12.64     12%
```
kevin: interesting that reads are many calls but small; writes are occasional but expensive. Maybe serialization on write path increases shared mem pressure.
anya: what's the smem occupancy per block?
mike: from nvprof sample: flash kernel uses ~48KB per block, 2 warps with dynamic offsets; occupancy dips to 25% on T4-like SMs.
emily: do we still fuse the kv write into the attention epilogue? I thought we switched to async stores last month.
dmitri: we did for the large batch path, but kernel_selector picks fused epilogue for seq>512 and when kv_enabled=true — heuristics might be wrong for small batch counts.
kevin: got it. Hypothesis: kernel_selector chooses fused epilogue to reduce global writes, but fused routine increases SMEM usage and causes bank conflicts when interleaved with KV writes from other warps -> stalls.
anya: what do traces show about memory stalls?
mike: perfetto shows high SMEM stall fraction (SMEM_STALL on perf counters) aligned with a bunch of __shfl_sync and atomic ops in the epilogue. Also we see serialization gaps between flash_attn_fused_rw_kernel invocations.
emily: can you try forcing the non-fused variant with the env var we added? (--REDWOOD_KERNEL_FUSE=0)
mike: tried that: total latency drops ~28% and SMEM stalls disappear from perfetto timeline. Results:
```
batch=2 seq=1024 kv=on
fused: 12.4ms/token
unfused: 8.9ms/token
```
dmitri: wow that's significant. So fused helps in large batches but hurts small-batch+kv cases. We need a selector rule.
kevin: propose: if kv_enabled && batch <= 4 && seq >= 768 then avoid fused epilogue on SM archs <= 8.0 or when smem_alloc>40KB.
anya: plus add a cheap micro-benchmark at startup to sample SMEM bank conflict behavior? Maybe run a tiny kernel that exercises typical access patterns and measure bank conflict counter. Add to warmup when kvEnabled.
emily: also add a telemetry flag so we can see how often selector picks fused for small batches in production. Tag routes with model, batch distribution.
dmitri: agree. I'll add a guard in kernel_selector and a quick perf counter probe (uses cupti) gated behind an opt-in env var. Also add a canary rollout: 10% traffic falls back to unfused for small batches to validate in prod.
mike: filing a tracker: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2987 — summary: SMEM affinity bank conflicts from fused-attn+kv-write path cause perf regression under small-batch kv workloads.
emily: ping me on the ticket for telemetry schemas.
kevin: one more ask: include the perfetto flame with overlayed counter tracks (SMEM_STALL, DRAM%). That helped us see the exact overlap.
mike: will attach traces and nvprof + a minimal repro harness (batch=2, seq=1024, kv=warm) to the ticket. Also add a simple unit test that forces both paths and asserts latency difference within 10% for small-batch kv workloads — to catch regressions.
anya: nice triage. If we can get a selector patch + telemetry today, we should have a canary by tomorrow. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: scheduled nsys nightly job with REDWOOD_KERNEL_FUSE=0 at 03:00 UTC for baseline collect.
emily: thanks all — bump the ticket when the selector PR is ready.
